items.title: Data races in the PFCP stack: its maps are used by the N4 receive threads and the N4 task without a lock
items.body:
### Description

The SMF PFCP stack is the same code as the UPF one (openairinterface/oai-cn5g-upf#44): `pfcp::pfcp_l4_stack` keeps a sequence number and four `std::map`s (`trxn_id2seq_num`, `proc_cleanup_timers`, `msg_out_retry_timers`, `pending_procedures`) with no lock (`src/pfcp/pfcp.hpp`, develop b2374073).

Several SMF threads change them at the same time:

- the receive threads of the two N4 sockets (`udp_s_8805` and `udp_s_allocated`), which call `handle_receive_message_cb()` for every message;
- the N4 task (`smf_n4_task`), which sends heartbeat requests (`smf_n4::send_heartbeat_request()`), sends the session requests and handles PFCP time-outs (`time_out_event()`).

Concurrent inserts and erases on one `std::map` are undefined behaviour and can corrupt the tree.

`itti_mw::increment_timer_id()` also does `return ++timer_id;` without the `m_timer_id` mutex that `itti_mw` has for it (`src/itti/itti.cpp`), so two threads can get the same timer ID.

### Expected behavior

The PFCP stack and the ITTI timer IDs are safe to use from these threads.

### Observed behavior

- On an OAI RF simulator testbed (OAI gNB and 4 nrUEs, official v2.2.2 AMF and UPF, `enable_urr: yes` in the UPF, SMF restarted twice and UEs restarted), `oai-smf` v2.2.2 built with `-fsanitize=thread` reported **120** data races in steady state on the `pfcp_l4_stack` state, between the N4 receive threads and `smf_n4_task`, including inserts and erases on the same `std::map`. `src/pfcp` and `src/itti` are the same on v2.2.2 and develop.
- The official `oai-smf:v2.2.2` image stopped once with SIGSEGV on the same testbed while the SMF was idle (only PFCP heartbeats in both directions and URR usage reports were running). The kernel log gives `segfault at 10 ... in libstdc++.so.6.0.33`; with the image's libstdc++ this address is in `std::_Rb_tree_insert_and_rebalance()`, which a valid tree does not crash in. No core dump was kept, so we cannot say which map was corrupted.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build `oai-smf` with `CXXFLAGS="-fsanitize=thread -g" LDFLAGS="-fsanitize=thread"` and add `libtsan2` to the image. Run it with `TSAN_OPTIONS="halt_on_error=0 log_path=..."`.
2. Start the core with a UPF that sends heartbeats and usage reports, and attach UEs.
3. Read the TSAN log after a few minutes.

A fix follows in a pull request; it is the same change as openairinterface/oai-cn5g-upf#45.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5-5
